A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same factuality-metric evaluation study. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original shallow-model comparisons, metric correlations, controlled summary manipulations, gaming experiments, and scoring with versus without source context.

after.justification: v4 reports original difficulty-stratified metric evaluations, controlled manipulations, gaming results, and factual versus counterfactual reference experiments.

M1.justification: The diagnostic procedure changes substantially. v1 evaluates a shallow classifier as a factuality scorer and separately trains a metric-score regressor; v4 removes the regression probe and uses classifier correctness and confidence to assign easy, medium, and hard examples. The shallow feature definitions and phrase-selection procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds ConflictBank evaluation with factual and counterfactual Wikipedia references and claims, introducing controlled conflicts between source support and world knowledge. v1 Appendix E instead evaluates summaries with versus without source context. Existing benchmark coverage is largely retained, with substantial train/test reassignment.

E2.justification: The six principal metrics in Table 1 are retained. QAFactEval, which has actual results in v1 Figure B.1, disappears with that analysis. The shallow MLP also ceases to appear as a directly scored comparator and instead determines the evaluation groups.

E3.justification: Table 3 substantially revises development/test assignments, including moving AggreFact datasets into training and all LLM-AggreFact datasets into testing. Evaluation adds confidence-based difficulty groups and four factual/counterfactual conditions. The reported ChatGPT-DA evaluator changes from GPT-4 to GPT-4o-mini. The benign-rewrite generator remains ambiguous because v4 Section 4.1 names GPT-4 while Appendix 11 names GPT-40-mini.

E4.justification: v4 adds difficulty-conditioned performance analysis and controlled testing of source support against factual truth. It removes v1's metric-score regression correlations, individual-feature correlation heatmap, and with/without-context analysis. Benign-edit tests and additional filler-phrase experiments remain, including the latter in v4 Figure 7.

E5.justification: v4 introduces a paired t-test comparing factual-reference and counterfactual-reference score gaps, reporting t=10.28 and p<0.001 in Section 4.2 and Figure 4. v1 has no corresponding significance test. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: v1's domain-level shallow-model comparisons and correlation results are replaced by difficulty-stratified AUCs; v4 reports AlignScore AUCs of 0.84, 0.68, and 0.49 across easy, medium, and hard groups. New counterfactual results show score gaps of 37.292 versus 26.901 and ranking-error rates of 0.2% versus 3.1%. ChatGPT manipulation results also change alongside the reported evaluator change, precluding same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v4 Section 3 introduces explicit difficulty definitions combining prediction correctness with confidence, measured by absolute deviation from 0.5, and 80%/20% percentile thresholds. This is a limited mathematical specification of the new diagnostic grouping. Neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The main shallow-feature claim changes from a supervised classifier being competitive with sophisticated metrics to all metrics deteriorating on examples difficult for that classifier. v4 also elevates ChatGPT-DA's relative robustness and dependence on parametric knowledge into central contributions, and adds explicit recommendations for benchmark and metric design.

C2.justification: v4 develops recommendations for difficulty- and severity-sensitive benchmarks, saliency-aware scoring, and testing source grounding. The parametric-knowledge concern already present in v1 Appendix E gains a more specific interpretation through counterfactual testing. v4 adds English-only and lack-of-mitigation limitations but removes caveats about supervised shallow-model comparisons, feature shallowness, and manual phrase selection.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses two MLP hidden layers of sizes 100 and 50, learning rate 0.001, and non-exhaustive spot-checking of benign edits; these disclosures do not establish architecture or checking-procedure changes. Conversely, it removes the 115-pair sample size and dataset provenance for the retained model-improvement comparison. Conflicting rewrite-model descriptions limit reproducibility.

R1.justification: v4 adds the ConflictBank citation and removes QAFactEval and FENICE references. Its dedicated Related Work section largely consolidates existing positioning, while adding an explicit contrast with Goyal and Durrett's analysis of error types. The broader relationship to previous factuality meta-evaluation remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, shallow-feature analysis, and concluding discussion are extensively rewritten. Feature descriptions move from Section 2.3 to Appendix 9, related work receives a dedicated section, and the conclusion becomes a recommendation-focused discussion. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. The domain-based AUC figure becomes difficulty panels, three diagnostic plots disappear, and a counterfactual-results figure is added. Gaming plots receive wider axes and rotated labels. Table 2 is shortened, while its full examples remain in Table 7; other tables and appendix figures are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The controlled ConflictBank experiment provides more direct evidence about grounding failures than v1's with/without-context score distributions. Difficulty-stratified evaluation and disclosed MLP settings also improve interpretability. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by conflicting rewrite-model descriptions, removal of sample details for a retained comparison, and loss of some methodological caveats.
